# K04. qkvx: the QKV-direct passes 1 and 2 under graph capture, and the RoPE backward with the QKV gradient's pre-/post-RHT amaxes (CUDA)

Classification: Internal (becomes public with the MLPerf Training v6.1 results)

[Index](../KERNELS.md) · Switches: `AK_QKV_DIRECT=1` (config L11), `AK_QKV_DIRECT_IMPL=cuda` (config L11), `AK_QKV_GRAD_AMAX=1` (config L10), and five version and direction knobs (`AK_QKVX_P1_VER`, `_P2_VER`, `_BWD_VER`, `AK_QKV_DIRECT_P1_REV`, `_P2_REV`; Enablement) · In the submitted runs: **on** (forward passes and backward) · Class: **E0** · Rule basis: Graph Execution (TR-8.3)

**L4 v3.** This item is L4 v2's, byte for byte, in L4 v3's image. Where this write-up names L4 v2's results, image or test runs, that evidence was collected on L4 v2's package (`firmus_gb300_ngpu8_llama8b_l4_nvfp4_v2`, withdrawn from this submission; see [Index](../KERNELS.md)). This package's own ten runs print the same first-call and ARMED lines, all `True` (Evidence).

## In brief

NVIDIA's recipe applies rotary position embedding (RoPE) to the packed QKV GEMM output with Transformer Engine's (TE's)
fused kernels; FP8 attention then quantizes q|k|v (amax pass, scale, cast), and the QKV gradient's NVFP4 quantize takes
two amaxes in a pass of its own. K04 (qkvx), a CUDA extension, (a) under CUDA-graph capture writes the per-position
maxima of the rotated q|k|v (pass 1) and the E4M3 bytes straight from the RoPE's inputs (pass 2), never writing the
bf16 q|k|v buffer; (b) in every backward writes the RoPE gradient and both amaxes in one pass for the gradient's
quantize. Every value comes from the same operations and rounding as the code it replaces (K01's RoPE arithmetic, TE's
saturating E4M3 cast, TE's own amax instructions); an amax does not depend on the order of its reduction. The passes
run only under capture; the in-run check runs them eagerly into scratch buffers.
**PASS:** this package's ten runs print every first-call check `True` and the kit passes on this image; the unit tests,
on L4 v2's image with the same binary (`23a2ac24`), found every byte equal to the stock path.

## What it replaces (Replaces)

Terms: **amax**, a tensor's largest absolute value, from which a quantizer derives its scale; **RHT**, TE's 16×16
random Hadamard transform, applied before NVFP4 quantization to the **column-wise copy** (the transposed copy the
weight-gradient GEMM reads); **pre-RHT amax**, the data's amax; **post-RHT amax**, that of the column-wise copy after
the RHT, in 16-token blocks. **CUDA-graph capture**: the recipe records the training iteration and the validation step
as CUDA graphs after an eager warm-up step, and every timed step replays them (`CUDA_GRAPH_IMPLEMENTATION="full_iteration"`, `config_common_cg.sh` L1; warm-up step 0 and the captures at `result_1.txt` L919-L925 and L942-L943).

**(a) The q|k|v forward, under CUDA-graph capture only.** NVIDIA's code: TE's `FusedQKVRoPEFunc.forward`
(`transformer_engine/pytorch/attention/rope.py`) calls `tex.fused_qkv_rope_forward`, which writes bf16 q, k and v; TE's
FP8 attention (`fp8_dpa`, current scaling) then quantizes them as one buffer with `Float8CurrentScalingQuantizer`: an
amax pass, the scale from the amax, the cast to E4M3. In this package an eager forward still writes the buffer: K02
(x12a) writes it with one partial maximum per (s, b) position, and K14 (fp8q) computes the scale from those maxima and
casts. Under capture K04 replaces both writes: pass 1 (`rope_fwd_partials`) writes only the partial maxima, K14's
`scale_from_partials` computes the scale from them (`ak_l8b_fp8cs_patch.py` L148), and pass 2 (`rope_fwd_fp8`) writes
the E4M3 bytes straight from the RoPE's inputs (`ak_l8b_fp8cs_patch.py` L149-150 → L90-92; patch `te/0001` L143-144,
L215-224). The bf16 buffer is not written in captured steps, because TE's FP8 attention keeps only the FP8 q, k and v.
These are K03's (x12d) two Triton passes, in CUDA; K03 is imported but never launched.

**(b) The RoPE backward and the gradient's amax pass, in every backward.** NVIDIA's code: `FusedQKVRoPEFunc.backward`
calls `tex.fused_qkv_rope_backward`, which writes the bf16 gradient of the packed QKV output; the QKV linear's NVFP4
quantize of that gradient (the recipe's RHT quantizer) then computes the pre-RHT and the post-RHT amax in a separate
Hadamard-amax pass. `rope_bwd_amax` writes the same gradient and, in the same pass, both amaxes (16×16 Hadamard, TE's
sign mask `0xd7e8`), and registers them with N06 (nvfp4p-patch, the NVFP4 patch module), whose next quantize of exactly
that tensor uses them instead of running the pass (patch `te/0001` L276-279, L181-187; `ak_l8b_nvfp4p_patch.py`
L1431-1447). The cast that consumes the amaxes is K12's (rht8) (`result_1.txt` L902).

A call outside the gate (Inputs it accepts) is not replaced by K04: a forward that K04's passes decline would get K03's
Triton passes under capture (never the case in the submitted runs); a backward K04 declines runs K01's (x12f) backward
kernel, and the gradient's quantize computes its amaxes itself; a call outside K01's hook gate runs TE's own kernels.

## Why the result is the same (Equivalence)

**Class E0: every output (FP8 bytes, `scale_inv`, the bf16 gradient and the two amaxes) is byte-identical to that of
the code it replaces.**

Notation: one head has D = 128 elements; `x_lo = x[0:64]` and `x_hi = x[64:128]` are its halves (likewise `g_lo`,
`g_hi` for a gradient). `f[d]` is the fp32 angle of element d at this position (the q angles for query heads, the k
angles for key heads); `cos_lo = cos(f[0:64])`, `cos_hi = cos(f[64:128])`, and likewise `sin_lo`, `sin_hi`. The angles
come from K01's table, `[s, 512]` fp32: cos and sin of the q angles, then of the k angles when they differ
(`ak_l8b_qkvx.cu` L14-16). Value heads are not rotated.

### The forward passes

NVIDIA's computation: per element of a q or k head, in fp32, rounded to bf16 when stored; then the FP8 quantize of the
stored buffer:

```
y[d]  = x[d]·cos(f[d]) − x[d+64]·sin(f[d])      d < 64
y[d]  = x[d]·cos(f[d]) + x[d−64]·sin(f[d])      d ≥ 64
amax  = max |y| over the whole q|k|v buffer (value heads: y = x)
out   = E4M3, round to nearest even, saturating, of float(y) · scale(amax)
```

This item (`rope_fwd8`, `ak_l8b_qkvx.cu` L73-87; `fp8x8`, L204-219):

```
y_lo  = bf16(fma(x_lo, cos_lo, (−x_hi)·sin_lo))       # __fmaf_rn, __fmul_rn
y_hi  = bf16(fma(x_hi, cos_hi,   x_lo ·sin_hi))
pass 1: part[s, b] = max |y| over the position's q, k and v heads   (nothing else is stored)
        scale      = K14's scale_from_partials(part)
pass 2: out = __nv_cvt_float2_to_fp8x2(float(y)·scale, __NV_SATFINITE, __NV_E4M3), at y's place in [q | k | v]
```

- The RoPE expression is the one of K01's and K02's Triton forward (`ak_l8b_qkvx.cu` L1-2, L14), with the same fma and
  the same round to nearest bf16 (`cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32`, `ak_l8b_rht_epi.cuh` L25).
- Pass 2 recomputes y from the same bf16 inputs with the same operations, so the bf16 value it converts is the one K02
  would have stored; it then does what TE's cast does to a stored element: `float(bf16) × scale`, round to nearest even,
  saturate to E4M3 (`ak_l8b_qkvx.cu` L12-13).
- Pass 1's partial maxima are maxima of the same bf16 values (L9-11), so their maximum is the buffer's amax. K14 derives
  the scale and `scale_inv` from it exactly as it does from K02's partials.

### The backward

NVIDIA's computation (`tex.fused_qkv_rope_backward`): per element of the gradient g of a q or k head, the sine is taken
at the rotated index and negated for the upper half; value-head gradients are copied. TE's NVFP4 gradient quantizer then
takes, of dx viewed as a `[s·b, h·(nq+2)·128]` matrix (h groups, nq query heads per group), two amaxes:

```
dx[d]  = g[d]·cos(f[d]) + g[d+64]·sin(f[d+64])     d < 64
dx[d]  = g[d]·cos(f[d]) − g[d−64]·sin(f[d−64])     d ≥ 64
a_pre  = max |dx|
a_post = max |bf16(T · dx_col)| over 16-token blocks of the column-wise copy,   T = diag(sign)·H16·0.25
```

This item (`rope_bwd8`, `ak_l8b_qkvx.cu` L57-71, and the epilogue `ak_l8b_rht_epi.cuh`):

```
y_lo   = bf16(fma(g_lo, cos_lo,   g_hi ·sin_hi))
y_hi   = bf16(fma(g_hi, cos_hi, (−g_lo)·sin_lo))
a_pre  : max.xorsign.abs.bf16x2 over the packed bf16 outputs
a_post : per 16-token × 16-feature sub-tile, mma.sync m16n8k16 (bf16 in, fp32 accumulate from zero) with T,
         then cvt.rn.bf16x2.f32 and max.xorsign.abs.bf16x2
both   : reduced in fp32 with max.f32 and a sign-bit mask, then an integer atomicMax per block
```

- `(−g_lo)·s` equals `g_lo·(−s)` exactly (negation is exact and IEEE multiplication is symmetric in sign), so the two
  lines are TE's two cases with the same products. This is K01's backward arithmetic (`ak_l8b_qkvx.cu` L3-4, L57-64).
- The amax instructions are TE's own (`ak_l8b_rht_epi.cuh` L1-11): the packed bf16 abs-max (L18-20); the post-RHT
  product by the HMMA that TE's `wmma m16n16k16` issues, with k = token as in TE (L6-9, L40-48); the bf16 rounding
  (L25); the fp32 reductions with no flush to zero (L10-11, L28-36); the publish by an integer `atomicMax` on the bits
  of non-negative floats, TE's `atomicMaxFloat` contract (L89-112). The RHT matrix entries are `sign[k]·H16[k][n]·0.25`,
  with `sign[k] = −1` where bit k of the mask is set (L53-58).
- The amaxes are taken of the bf16 outputs the pass writes, staged in shared memory for the RHT (`ak_l8b_qkvx.cu` L5-8).
  An amax is a maximum: its value does not depend on the order of the reduction or of the atomics.

### The hand-offs

- **Forward (to N10):** a packed forward registers the RoPE's inputs and the two passes as callables (`p1`, `p2`) in
  the registry `_AK_QKVA_REG` (patch `te/0001` L207-214). Under capture, once `direct_ok` is set, it runs only pass 1 and
  marks the buffer deferred (L215-224). N10's quantize of exactly that buffer (same pointer and size,
  `ak_l8b_fp8cs_patch.py` L73-84) then runs K14's scale and pass 2 (L140-157, L204-208). A quantize of any other tensor
  computes its own amax (K14's amax path with `AK_FP8CS_AMAX=1`, else the stock path; L197-201); a deferred buffer
  quantized outside capture raises (L204-206), and one left unquantized raises at the next packed forward (patch
  L205-206).
- **Backward (to N06):** the result is registered as `_STATE["bwd_reg"]`: a weak reference to the gradient, its version
  counter, the two amaxes, the sign mask and the site `rope_bwd` (patch L181-187). The next quantize call consumes or
  drops it (`ak_l8b_nvfp4p_patch.py` L1213-1214). It is used only for that tensor or a view of it, with the same pointer,
  size and version counter, contiguous bf16, the recipe's quantizer and the same RHT sign mask (L1211-1224); otherwise
  it is dropped and the stock amax pass runs (L1431-1434). K04's sign mask is `_STATE.get("rht_mask", 0xD7E8)` (patch
  L161); no code sets `rht_mask`, so it is TE's default `0xd7e8`, and the consumer requires the quantizer's mask to be
  the same (L1222).

**State kept between calls** ([index](../KERNELS.md#state-kept-between-calls-tr-83)): none in the kernel (each
`rope_bwd_amax` call allocates its gradient and a zeroed amax pair, `ak_l8b_qkvx.cu` L583-584; the passes write only
buffers the caller passes in). The wiring keeps the two single-use hand-offs above (the last packed q|k|v buffer's
pointer, size, partial maxima, pass callables and deferred mark; the gradient's registered amaxes), each cleared by the
quantize that takes it, plus once-only "checked" flags and call counters (patch `te/0001` L83-84, L129, L181-187,
L230-231; `ak_l8b_fp8cs_patch.py` L83, L167, L190-192; `ak_l8b_nvfp4p_patch.py` L1213-1214).

## Numerics (Numerics)

- bf16 in; fp32 arithmetic with explicit `__fmaf_rn` / `__fmul_rn` (no contraction is left to the compiler); one round
  to nearest bf16 per stored or converted value; no fast math (`-O3 -lineinfo`, `firmus/ak/build_manifest.json` L14).
- FP8: E4M3 with TE's per-tensor current scaling (the scale from the amax, computed by K14); round to nearest even,
  saturating (`__NV_SATFINITE`).
- Amaxes: fp32; the pre-RHT amax over the whole gradient, the post-RHT amax over 16-token blocks of the column-wise
  copy; no flush to zero. The formats are the recipe's own (Numerical formats, TR-5.2a): FP8 E4M3 current scaling for
  the attention inputs and NVFP4 for the QKV gradient. Nothing changes a format.

## Optimizer and gradient clipping (Optimizer, Gradient clipping)

Not applicable: an activation and activation-gradient op; it updates no parameter, and it neither computes nor applies the clip coefficient.

## Inputs it accepts (Shape specialisation)

### Gate

- **Hook gate** (K01's `_ak_x12_armed`, patch L33-35): `tensor_format == "sbhd"`, not interleaved, `cp_size == 1`, no
  start positions, bf16, 4-D; the forward tests `qkv`, the backward `grad_output_q`. Anything else runs TE's own kernels.
- **Forward passes** (`_ak_qkvx_direct`, patch L136-145): the extension loaded, `AK_QKV_DIRECT_IMPL=cuda`, head dim 128,
  micro-batch 1-4, a contiguous, 16-byte-aligned bf16 qkv; otherwise K03's Triton passes would be registered instead
  (they never are here). **Packed-forward assert** (patch L195): `total == qs + ks + vs`, `ks == vs == d`,
  `qs % d == 0`; a failure raises.
- **Backward** (`_ak_qkvg_backward`, patch L148-159): N06 armed with its hand-off slot (its `_STATE` holds `bwd_reg`);
  head dim 128; K and V widths equal to the head dim; `qs % d == 0`; an even number of query heads per group
  (`(nq + 2) % 2 == 0`); rows = s·b with rows % 32 == 0 and rows / 32 ≤ 65,535; dq, dk and dv bf16. Otherwise K01's
  backward kernel runs (patch L280-283), and the gradient's quantize computes its amaxes itself. With another hand-off
  pending, K04 still writes the gradient but does not register its amaxes (L181-187).
- **Versions** (patch L132-133): a configured version of 30 or more is used only for exactly the recipe's attention
  shape (8 key/value groups of 4 query + 2 key/value heads at micro-batch 2); any other shape, including any other head
  layout the gate admits, takes version 2. Versions other than the submitted ones, and version 2, are compiled in but
  never run with the submitted switches ([code present but not
  executed](../KERNELS.md#code-present-but-not-executed-with-the-submitted-switches)).
- **Kernel checks** (`ak_l8b_qkvx.cu`; each raises a `RuntimeError`): contiguous CUDA bf16 inputs (L557-560); the
  angle table contiguous fp32 `[≥ s, 512]` (L561-565); for the backward dq `[s, b, h·nq, 128]`, dk = dv `[s, b, h, 128]`,
  nq even, rows % 32 == 0, rows / 32 ≤ 65,535 and b ≤ 65,535 (L576-580); for pass 1 a micro-batch of 1-4 (L656); for
  pass 2 a contiguous `uint8` output with as many elements as qkv, 8-byte aligned (L713-715); for version 2, heads per
  token a multiple of 4 (backward, L619) and at most 192 head-rows per position (passes, L645-649, L685, L742).
- **Version 3** (versions 30-39 backward, 30-38 passes; L424-432): version 2 with the recipe's shape compiled in (h 8,
  nq 4, b 2: every index a compile-time constant) and the CTA shape as a template parameter; the kernel itself refuses
  version 3 at another shape (L591, L664, L720). All versions call the same device functions for the arithmetic
  (`rope_bwd8`, `rope_fwd8`, `fp8x8` and the epilogue) and differ in how threads and tiles are laid out (L259-266,
  L424-432). Walk direction (`AK_QKV_DIRECT_P1_REV`, `AK_QKV_DIRECT_P2_REV`): the order in which the CTAs take the
  sequence positions (`kRev`: from the end, L145, L159); every position is computed the same way.
  The submitted versions: backward 34 (16 tokens × 4 heads per CTA, at least 6 CTAs per SM;
  L430, L604), passes 37 and 37 (96 threads, at least 5 CTAs per SM;
  L431-432, L674, L731).
- **Training call:** qkv (8192, 2, 8, 768), split [512, 128, 128], freqs (8192, 1, 1, 128) (`result_1.txt` L867); a
  q|k|v buffer of 100,663,296 elements (L870); dqkv [8192, 2, 8, 768], quantized as [16384, 6144] (L900, L903).
  Evaluation forwards have the same micro-batch 2 (the validation warm-up's lines show [8192, 2, 4096], L935) and are
  captured too (L942-L943).

### Assumptions not checked in code

- **The unwritten buffer has one reader.** Under capture, the bf16 q, k and v views that TE receives are views of a
  buffer that is allocated but never written. The patch relies on TE's FP8 attention (current scaling, O in F16) saving
  only the FP8 q, k, v and reading the buffer only through the one quantize (patch L93-95). No code checks that nothing
  else reads q, k or v: the checks catch only a buffer never quantized (patch L205-206) and a deferred buffer quantized
  outside capture (`ak_l8b_fp8cs_patch.py` L204-206), both of which raise. What keeps it true here: FP8 attention is on
  (`FP8_DPA=True`, `config_common_fp8attn.sh` L1), and its only use of q|k|v is that quantize. If another op read the
  views under capture, it would read uninitialised memory: a **silent wrong result**.
- **One check per process.** N10's check of the passes runs once (`direct_checked`, `ak_l8b_fp8cs_patch.py` L167,
  L211), K04's amax check once (`_AK_QKVG["checked"]`, patch L165-166), and the consuming quantize's check once per
  (site, row-wise, column-wise, stochastic rounding) key (`ak_l8b_nvfp4p_patch.py` L1444-1448). A later call with
  another shape, angle table or quantizer format runs without an in-run comparison (pass 2 always writes E4M3; the check
  requires E4M3 once). The passes' check runs on whichever passes the first buffer takes (K04's in the submitted runs),
  so a later captured buffer that K04's passes declined would run K03's passes unchecked. What keeps it true here:
  training and evaluation send one q|k|v shape, and training one gradient shape (Gate, "Training call"). If it failed,
  a wrong result would be **silent**.
- **Version 3's grid.** The backward's gate checks rows / 32 ≤ 65,535 (patch L157; `ak_l8b_qkvx.cu` L580), but version
  3 launches rows / 16 blocks in the grid's y dimension (L596, L604), whose limit is 65,535: with version 3 (b = 2), a
  sequence of more than 524,280 positions would fail at launch, and `C10_CUDA_KERNEL_LAUNCH_CHECK` (L615) **raises**.
  Training has 16,384 rows.
- **The angle table.** K04 reads the table K01 builds from the frequency tensors (patch L160, L202); `check_tab` checks
  only its dtype and shape. Its layout, and the frequency tensor's layout that K01 assumes, are K01's (K01, "Assumptions
  not checked in code"); a wrong table would give a **silent wrong result** here as in K01.

### Benchmark detection

The gate and the kernel checks test only tensor layout, dtype, dimensions and alignment, and the switches. Version 3 is
chosen by tensor dimensions (groups, heads per group, micro-batch), not by the benchmark's identity; any other shape
takes version 2, which uses the same device functions. Nothing reads the program's name or the benchmark (Benchmark
detection, TR-2.3).

## How it is switched on and checked at run time (Enablement)

- **Switches** (config L10-12), all read by patch `te/0001` at TE import:

  | switch | value | read at | default | effect |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `AK_QKV_DIRECT` | `1` | patch L96 | `0` | QKV direct on; effective only with `AK_QKV_AMAX=1` (K02); also imports K03's Triton passes (L100-102) |
  | `AK_QKV_DIRECT_IMPL` | `cuda` | L118 | `triton` | `cuda` selects this item's passes |
  | `AK_QKVX_P1_VER`, `AK_QKVX_P2_VER` | `37`, `37` | L124-125 | `2` | versions of pass 1 and pass 2 |
  | `AK_QKV_DIRECT_P1_REV`, `AK_QKV_DIRECT_P2_REV` | `0`, `1` | L119-120 | `0`, `1` | walk direction of each pass |
  | `AK_QKVX_BWD_VER` | `34` | L123 | `2` | version of the backward |
  | `AK_QKV_GRAD_AMAX` | `1` | L117 | `0` | the backward with the amaxes on |

- **Other items' switches it needs:** `AK_X12_ROPE=1` (K01), `AK_QKV_PACK=1`
  (N01), `AK_QKV_AMAX=1` (K02), `AK_FP8CS=1` (N10),
  `AK_NVFP4P=1` (N06) and `AK_NVFP4P_BX=1` (K13: without it `_ext_b()`
  raises, `ak_l8b_nvfp4p_patch.py` L224-226).
- **Import:** when `AK_X12_ROPE` is on and either `AK_QKV_GRAD_AMAX`, or `AK_QKV_DIRECT` with
  `AK_QKV_DIRECT_IMPL=cuda`, is on, the patch imports `ak_l8b_qkvx` at TE import from `AK_X12_KERNEL_DIR`, which it puts
  on `sys.path` (patch L27-29, L127-128). An ImportError raises; there is no fallback.
- **First-call check of the passes:** N10's eager check (`ak_l8b_fp8cs_patch.py` L165-192) runs at the first eager
  quantize of a registered (written) buffer (L211). It runs pass 1 and pass 2, the same callables that run under capture,
  into scratch buffers and compares the FP8 bytes and `scale_inv` with TE's own quantize of the written buffer, the amax
  with the maximum of the written path's (K02's) partial maxima (L176-178), and the format (E4M3); it also reports,
  without requiring it, whether pass 1's partials equal K02's ("an all-NaN position may differ", L180). A mismatch raises
  (L188-189). Only a match sets `direct_ok` (L190-192); without it, captured forwards keep writing the buffer (patch
  L215, L225-229).
- **First-call checks of the backward:** the first eager call compares the two amaxes bit for bit (as int32) with K13's
  (nvfp4bx) `rht_amax` of the same gradient (patch L165-180, through `_ext_b()`, `ak_l8b_nvfp4p_patch.py` L222-232,
  which loads `ak_l8b_nvfp4bx`), at the binding's default version 2 (`ak_l8b_nvfp4bx.cu` L865-866), the version K13's
  own site runs by code default. The printed text "bit-equal to ak_l8b_nvfp4b.rht_amax" is fixed in the code (patch
  L173-174); `ak_l8b_nvfp4b` is not in this build ([modules not
  shipped](../KERNELS.md#7-training-evidence-and-modules-not-shipped)). In the same eager call, K01's backward first-call
  check compares the gradient byte for byte with `tex.fused_qkv_rope_backward` (patch L285-289). The quantize that
  consumes the amaxes is compared with TE's `tex.quantize` at its first eager call, with the RNG state restored for
  stochastic rounding (`ak_l8b_nvfp4p_patch.py` L1443-1467). Each mismatch raises.
- **Run-start gate:** no row of its own. The "fp8cs" row (`firmus_ak/run_start_gate.py` L50-52) passes once any of N10's paths is checked; the "x12 rope" row (L89-93) requires K01's forward and backward first-call checks, and the backward check runs in the same eager call as K04's amax check. The gate's verdict is per rank ([enablement and fail-loud behaviour](../KERNELS.md#enablement-and-fail-loud-behaviour)).
- **Log lines:** rank 0 prints one ARMED line for the passes and one for the backward; the checks run on every rank (Evidence, "Checks in every scored run").

## Approval (Approval)

None needed: E0. Graph Execution (TR-8.3) allows mathematically equivalent changes to the non-weight parts of the
computation; the FP8 and NVFP4 formats are the recipe's (Numerical formats, TR-5.2a).

## Evidence (Evidence)

**Result on the submitted image:** PASS: in each of this package's ten runs the QKV-direct, gradient-amax,
RoPE-backward and consuming-quantize first-call lines are `True`, and the kit for this kernel passes on this image; the
unit tests, on L4 v2's image with the same binary, equal the stock path byte for byte (below).

### Tests on the submitted image

- The image's build of `ak_l8b_qkvx.cu` gave the same binary as L4 v2's, `23a2ac24` (record R7). The install check and
  the import and banner tests passed ([tests on the built image](../KERNELS.md#5-tests-on-the-built-image)).
- **The smoke** of the submitted config (2 × 4 GPUs; record R18) printed the QKV-direct, gradient-amax, RoPE-backward
  and consuming-quantize lines at the same line numbers as the runs, all `True`, and the gate's line over 19 parts.
- **The kit for this kernel: PASS** in both forms, as written and after a random-byte fill of PyTorch's memory pools
  (six tests, each exit 0; records R1-R3). Its sha checks show that it loads the image's `ak_l8b_qkvx.so` (`23a2ac24`),
  Triton files `fused_qkv_rope_amax.py` (`3ad20067`) and `fused_qkv_rope_fp8.py` (`8d378708`), K14's `ak_l8b_fp8q.so`
  (`7c5815e0`), the installed `rope.py` (`c4d98fb9`) and N10's patch module (`1aca679a`). It runs:
  - two byte tests of the passes and the backward (16 and 28 checks per input case; shared and separate q/k angles;
    Gaussian, NaN, huge and subnormal inputs): no failure;
  - the QKV-direct self-tests, through the image's N10 module: passes 1 and 2 at versions 30 / 31 and at the submitted
    37 / 37 against TE's quantize of the written buffer, eager and under CUDA graphs (with a second replay);
  - the gradient-amax self-tests, an end-to-end layer (LayerNormLinear → RoPE → backward, with the backward at version
    34): the path with the registered amaxes against the path with the RHT-amax pass, the input gradient and two
    parameter gradients equal for seeds 11-13, eager and under CUDA graphs. Their RHT-amax reference is the kit's own
    copy of the dropped module `ak_l8b_nvfp4b` (`c34d419a`), loaded by an earlier NVFP4P patch module that the kit arms
    (`37ea564d`), not the image's `ak_l8b_nvfp4bx`; their RHT casts are the kit's `ak_l8b_rht6` (`0500fac0`), not K12's
    `ak_l8b_rht8`; their RoPE ARMED line (K01's) names the earlier `fused_qkv_rope.py` `a91b35c1`, not the image's K01
    module (`891457a5`, `result_1.txt` L867). Their first-call lines are against TE (K01's forward and backward checks,
    the consuming quantize) or against that kit copy (K04's amax line); the scored runs' amax check uses the image's
    `ak_l8b_nvfp4bx` (Enablement).

### Tests on L4 v2's image

L4 v2's submitted image; its files differ from L4 v3's only in N11's module, the run-start gate, the leaf's one added
switch, four comments or docstrings, and the three rebuilt extensions (K10, K11, K12).

- **Bytes:** the image's `/opt/firmus/ak/x12/ak_l8b_qkvx.so`, `23a2ac24d5056967`: MATCH. Every test below ran in that
  image with no file mounted over it and armed the image's own modules with its leaf's switches (record R8).
- **Forward unit test: PASS** (records R8, R12): K02's partial maxima (eager forwards) and K04's passes 1 and 2 with
  K14's scale at the direct site, run as a captured graph replayed per case (the forward of every timed step), against
  the stock path on visible, reseeded, hidden, shape-variant and edge cases.
- **Backward unit test: PASS** (records R8, R12): `rope_bwd_amax` and the quantize with the registered amaxes, captured
  and replayed on new inputs, against the stock path on the same case families: every byte equal.
- **Address independence and the mixed eager / capture / replay sequence: PASS**, forward and backward (records R8,
  R13). The backward's replays are graded against the stock path's own replay: 0 bytes differ (stochastic rounding
  makes a replay's FP4 data, row-wise and column-wise, differ from the eager result, in the stock path too). The forward
  test's own capture warm-up runs on a side stream it forks and joins (the scale kernel, K02's kernel and the cast, not
  K04's), declared to the check.
- **Coverage check** (record R14): every path K04 runs is graded: passes 1 and 2 by the forward unit test and its
  address and mixed-sequence check, `rope_bwd_amax` by the backward unit test and its own such check. An earlier run of
  the unit tests and the kit on the image's own bytes also graded every byte equal (record R11).
